extracted.intended_audience: writers of short/periodical essays and moral/polemical pieces
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing concise, engaging periodical essays (single-sheet papers) that must be immediately engaging, conceptually complete, and morally or intellectually useful. Emphasises compactness, novelty, and fitting content to the publication format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate opening and lively treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: “We must immediately fall into our Subject, and treat every Part of it in a lively Manner, or our papers are thrown by as dull and insipid.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin promptly with the subject; each short piece must engage the reader at once and keep a lively tone throughout, otherwise it risks being discarded by periodical readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual completeness despite brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: “every Sheet should be a kind of Treatise, and make out in Thought what it wants in Bulk.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single-page or short essay should present a self-contained argument or exploration: compensate for lack of physical length by ensuring the idea is fully formed and developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Density and novelty of matter or expression
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our Matter must lie close together, and either be wholly new in itself, or in the Turn it receives from our Expressions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pack content tightly; the piece should offer new information or at least a fresh phrasing/angle so that the reader feels rewarded by the concise presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repetition, tautology, and enlargement
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects should be handled “without the Repetitions, Tautologies and Enlargements, that are indulged to longer Labours.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elide needless restatement and expansion that are acceptable in larger volumes; aim for precision and economy of words in periodical pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fully develop a point of humour
rubrics_metrics.description: “That a Point of Humour should be worked up in all its Parts.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the essay aims to be humorous, the comic idea must be elaborated and executed completely within the short space, not left as a loose hint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distill the essence (the ‘Chymical Method’)
rubrics_metrics.description: “An Essay-Writer must practise in the Chymical Method, and give the Virtue of a full Draught in a few Drops.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use compression and careful selection so the piece delivers the power and effect of a longer work in very small compass; every sentence must contribute to the concentrated effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match form to expectations (volume vs separate sheets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors publishing in volumes may “be dull sometimes” and enjoy allowances for rest and preamble, whereas separate sheets “have none of these Advantages.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate format for the material: longer, digressive treatments suit collected volumes; periodical sheets demand immediacy, focus, and momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social/intellectual purpose: instruct and edify
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be “calculated to diffuse good Sense through the Bulk of a People, to clear up their Understandings, animate their Minds with Virtue, dissipate the Sorrows of a heavy Heart, or unbend the Mind from its more severe Employments with innocent Amusements.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to inform, morally uplift, relieve sorrow, or pleasantly entertain — periodical essays serve a public function and should strive to improve or lighten readers’ minds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept audience variation; don’t be discouraged by poor readers
rubrics_metrics.description: “I am not at all mortified, when sometimes I see my Works thrown aside by Men of no Taste nor Learning… Their Souls are not to be enlightened.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that some readers will fail to appreciate subtleties; target the audience likely to benefit and be sustained despite indifference or hostile criticism from less discerning readers.
